title: Step-duration crumb traces and cache influence instrumentation
creator: Jordan Patel
description:
Goal: add very low-overhead per-emission step timing ('crumb') traces and lightweight cache-influence annotations so we can attribute millis and cost deltas to micro-steps of a request without overwhelming ingestion pipelines.

Rationale: current telemetry shows request-level and token-aggregate latencies but cannot explain which micro-step (tokenization, kv lookup, kernel exec, post-processing, network enqueue) contributed most to tail latency or cost. This ticket introduces a minimal, sampled microspan model that can be merged with existing tracing and metrics to produce per-slot latency and per-token cost breakouts including cache-hit vs cache-miss delta.

Scope: implement runtime probes that emit a stamped 'crumb' for each logical step in the emission pipeline. Each crumb is 1) small (O(50-200 bytes) when sampled), 2) correlated with request_id, sequence_slot, model_variant, and kv_cache_tag, and 3) encoded for downstream enrichment in metrics/log pipelines. The runtime will expose a dynamic sampling knob (global and per-tenant overrides). Backend work: enrich log/metric collectors to reconstruct per-token timelines, compute cache-hit latency deltas, and feed results into a new dashboard and nightly QA job that recalculates token-level unit economics.

Non-goals: full-fidelity per-token traces for 100% traffic (costly); replacing existing token attribution pipelines (this augments them).

Implementation notes:
- Instrumentation points: pre-tokenize, post-tokenize, before-kv-read, after-kv-read (with hit/miss flag), pre-kernel, post-kernel, before-decode, after-emit.
- Emission format: tombstone-free binary protobuf with a compact header containing request_id, slot_index, ts_ns, step_id, step_duration_ns (optional), and flags. Fallback JSON encoding for Dev mode.
- Sampling: probabilistic per-request sampling (default 0.5%) + on-demand trace for canaries. Sampling metadata included in crumb so pipelines can extrapolate totals.
- Low overhead: when not sampled, runtime will still increment internal counters but will not allocate spans or proto objects. Avoid locks on hot path; use per-worker ring buffers and batched flush.
- Correlation: attach crumb_id and parent_request_id to existing OpenTelemetry spans so traces can be stitched in the console and the denormalized timeline can be computed offline.

Deliverables:
1) runtime changes (C++/Rust) to emit crumb records with sampling knobs.
2) collector + enrichment pipeline updates (Kafka/Fluentd -> Spark job) to compute per-token timelines and cache-influence deltas.
3) dashboards: latency by step, distribution by slot index, cache hit vs miss latency delta, token-level cost heatmap.
4) regression tests and a canary run on dedicated capacity for 72h with traffic replay.

Privacy & compliance: crumbs omit customer prompt text and only include cryptographic prompt-hash to link to an eval bucket. No plaintext customer data in crumb payloads.
acceptance_criteria: Runtime emits crumb records for the listed instrumentation points when sampling is enabled
Crumbs include request_id, slot_index, step_id, timestamp, and hit/miss flag for kv reads
Collector pipeline reconstructs per-slot timelines for sampled requests and stores aggregated per-slot histograms
Dashboard surfaces step-level p50/p95/p99 latencies by slot index and cache-hit vs cache-miss deltas
Overhead measured in canary: <1% p95 latency increase and <2% CPU on typical dedicated instance at default sampling
Unit economics job computes token-level cost delta attributable to cache misses and is validated against synthetic traces
tasks: Design crumb proto and sampling metadata
Implement runtime emission hooks with per-worker batching
Add dynamic sampling config in control plane and SDK
Collector: schema change + enrichment job to stitch crumbs into timelines
Create dashboards and add alerts for unexpected spike in cache-miss delta
End-to-end tests with traffic replay and synthetic cache-hit/miss scenarios
Ship canary and monitor overhead + correctness for 72h
comments: 2025-02-14 Jordan Patel: Spike complete. Proposed proto attached in links. Initial perf estimate ~6 points. Priority set to P1 due to upcoming SRE request.
2025-02-18 Riley Chen: Prototype of pre/post kernel hooks implemented on branch feat/crumbs. Needs review for lock-free buffering approach.
2025-02-24 Devon Li (SRE): Keep default sampling low for hosted customers. We saw ingestion bursts in a similar project; recommend rate-limiter on the collector tier.
2025-03-01 Design review: UX team prefers showing reconstructed timeline as stacked bars per-token with hover breakdown (step+duration). Avoid exposing raw crumb IDs in UI.
2025-03-04 Riley Chen: Updated tasks to include canary plan. Added dashboard KPIs and alert thresholds. Marking ready for implementation.
Reviewer notes: ensure crumb payloads do not contain prompt text. Add e2e test that verifies no user content is present in emitted crumb records.
